questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my Spanish! And I love outdoor activites like hiking, trekking and camping and have had a big wish for a long time to visit chile. Also safety wise it was one of the safer countries in LATAM.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I loved Chile!
Beautiful country, the chileans are really nice and was generally happy about my exchange. Downside was quite a lot of time needed to be spend on school (mostly for architecture it sounds like, friends from economy, social science etc barely had any work)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: My coordinator at Uchile was really helpful, and answered fast on both email and it was possible to show up at his office. There was a lot of different (and lacking) information about my orientation at the faculty of architecture, but through talking to other architecture students i got the lacking information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: PME (my faculty) was a big help with questions etc. There was an orientation for exchange students which was a nice intro to the school and other students. It was confusing because I had classes at FAU, but didnt get the emails from them because my faculty was PME, so I missed quite a lot of important information I had to find out through the other architecture students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Really easy!
Don't stress about finding housing before arriving, and dont necessarily book something before coming there. I came 3 weeks before my school started to find housing, and i was so nice to visit the different neighborhoods and get the feeling of where you want to live and visit the places.
for info! Santiago is super cold in winter, and a lot of student housing + classrooms + restaurants dont have heating. So bring warm clothes!! and a 'varmedunk' for sleeping at night in a cold house is key.
I found my housing through
https://www.compartodepto.cl/
and lived with 9 other exchange students and 4 chileans. My rent was 300.000 a month. I was generally happy about my housing situation, but there was really strict house rules, which in retrospect, I would rather have lived in a house with more chill rules. We weren't allowed visitors after 20:00 and not allowed to have many people over.
Depending on what you want, I think the nicest housing situtions were the houses located with between 6-14 people living together without too many rules. Many exchange peoples main friend group were there house, and you can find places with not too many strict rules and not too expensive. Downside is a lot of europeans lives in these houses (bad if you want to speak/improve spanish), but there were also housing with south americans/chileans.
Other places to look are
https://www.rumi4students.com/

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nobody lived on campus so weren't really a problem. But check where your campus is! I could walk to my campus and loved it. Santiago is well-connected by buses/metro, but can be time consuming because of heavy traffic.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally cheap and easy to find housing compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
A bit stressfull and confusing. 
At my faculty, FAU, we had to wish for courses before coming to chile, but when school started we had to attend all the classes we wanted to have, and ask the teacher if we could join the class. The teachers was often confused about whether we could join the class or not, and I feel like there was a lot of back and forth between the exchange office and the teachers. Some classes were also only allowed 3 exchange students per class, but the rules were bended in some cases and there were a lot more.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Talk with the exchange coordinator at your faculty - they can sometimes help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try not to stress, you will find courses even though the process is very confusing. And talk with the teachers and show interest for their course! I feel like a lot of them like excange students in general and wants to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally really passionate teachers and had some nice classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level itself wasn't too difficult. The big challenge for me was having all of my courses in spanish (ecspecially chilean spanish). I barely understood anything when I arrived.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: a lot of tests with paper and pens, which is very different from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I had Geografia Urbana, Taller 7, espanol para extranjeros and Experimentos
Urbanos: Estudios de Impacto del Entono Construido en el
Comportamiento Humano

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I loved geografia urbana! A lot of interesting knowledge about city development, also in santiago, and there was a 4 day field trip where i got my first chilean friends. In general try to pick the courses with field trips, 
Taller 7 was also nice because my professor (saveedra) was amazing. When choosing a taller ask the chilean students for which teachers are nice (and maybe understanding towards exchange students that are trying to learn spanish still or miss class sometimes because they travel etc.)
There is also an instagram run by students at FAU called ayuditasfau where there are comments about the different teachers and courses. 

I dont recomment experimentos urbanos, too much statistics and a LOT of work outside class. Spanish was okay (if you get ECTS points for it), but didnt learn the most there because the classes were to big (17 students).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general there wasn't any unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries are quite expensive in the supermarket, like danish prices. But you can get cheap vegetables if you go to the ferias (markets) like vega central.

Sport is really cheap! I bouldered, played padel and squash for 1/4 to 1/2 of the price in denmark. Enjoy with new friends!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In FAU there weren't that many clubs/sports (only football, basket, volley), but there was a really nice social student environment with boardgame club, friday bar each friday after class, and a lot of architecutre talks etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In FAU there weren't that many clubs/sports (only football, basket, volley), but there was a really nice social student environment with boardgame club, friday bar each friday after class, and a lot of architecutre talks etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is salsa class for 15 DKK each tuesday, wednessday and thursday next to GAM at 8 pm. We loved it and went many times. Cinema is really cheap, sport is really cheap and there are a lot of free museums. Parts of the roads closes from sunday 9-14:00 so people can bike/run/etc and a nice way to run and see the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I loved travelling and hiking around in chile!
there are a lot of hikes just at the edge of the city, and also national parks easily accesible. 
Remember a credit card from back home so you can rent a car and drive around! we went on many roadtrips outside of chile, and drove around, and it felt safe enough.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy. The chileans are generally really sweet and welcoming. 
The only difference I really felt ws in the work culture. Much of my group work we had meetings after 22:00/23:00/00:00 at night, and it wasn't unusual for my group members to work during the night often. 
Also when making plans to meet for example at campus to work, people was most often 1-2 hours late, or didnt show up. So pack away the danish puntualism and start being a bit late as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Take the first step! 
The chileans are sweet and welcoming, but I often felt like I had to take a small first step to talk to them, or invite them to something, and then they almost immediately started inviting me to events, make plans afterwards etc.
Made most of my chilean friends through field trips in classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The working hours. And also communicating in spanish. the young chileans use a lot of slang (but they will happily learn you some).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How funny chileans are. They are real joksters. Also how inviting they are, me and my friend got invited on trips, home to peoples familys houses without knowing people THAT well. It was really nice. And they love to show you their culture! Ask for where to learn Cueca for festias patrias or where to get the best completo.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to get chilean friends. Some of my best culturally experiences and friendsships where because I got to know them . My spanish was too bad the first 2 months to properly get to know people in spanish, but I tried and practised and in the last past of my semester i felt more confident speaking in spanish with them.

2. Get out of Santiago! Santiago is amazing and has a lot of cultural offers, but Chile is so much more than santiago. Go north, go south and explore with friends and see the amazing nature. I have never seen so much pretty nature as here in chile. 

3. Be open to people and opportunities, and invite people to the stuff you want to do! Often they want to join. Even though it was nice having chilean friends, it was also really nice having friends on exchange that wanted to do stuff with you, and also explore chile!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Mentioned earlier. But in general talk with the office if in doubt about anything academic!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a new language, seeing beautiful nature and getting to know a lot of lovely people. I also love getting to know the chilean culture like learning to dance cueca for 18 sept, learning about chiles history etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely having the classes and a life in spanish!! At times I was really frustrated when I didn't quite understand what was going on because of the language, I was short on time and had a test, and everything felt so difficult. But it all resolved everytime.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Goooo! Chile was nice.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
